subject: Food Science
title: Bioterrorism and Food Defense
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bioterrorism and Food Defense.

hook.text: In 1984, a cult in Oregon contaminated 10 salad bars with Salmonella. 751 people were sickened—the first US bioterror food attack.

buildup.text: Food defense protects against intentional contamination—terrorism, sabotage, or disgruntled employees tampering with products.

discovery.text: The FDA's CARVER+Shock method identifies food supply chain points most vulnerable to deliberate tampering.

twist.text: Open salad bars, buffets, and bulk bins are the most vulnerable. Any customer could contaminate food that hundreds eat.

climax.text: Tamper-evident packaging became standard after 7 died from cyanide-laced Tylenol in 1982. That case changed all packaging.

punchline.text: Food defense plans for the unthinkable. Intentional contamination, intentional prevention.

quiz.question: What event led to tamper-evident packaging becoming standard?
options: The 1982 cyanide-laced Tylenol deaths in Chicago
